title: Tag list defaults
prompt: add_tag(tag, tags=[]) adds a tag to a list. Each call without a tags argument should start from an empty list, but tags from earlier calls keep appearing.
starter:
def add_tag(tag, tags=[]):
    # add_tag("x") -> ["x"]; add_tag("y") -> ["y"]
    # add_tag("z", ["a"]) -> ["a", "z"]
    tags.append(tag)
    return tags
hints: Call add_tag('x') twice in Run. Why does the second result have two items?
A default value is created once, when the def line runs, and the same list object is shared by every call.
Use tags=None as the default and create a new [] inside the function when tags is None.
explanation: The default list is created once at definition time and shared by every call, so tags piled up between calls. The fix is a None default and a new list inside the function.
